subject: Food Science
title: Koji: The Master Mold
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Koji: The Master Mold.

hook.text: Soy sauce, miso, sake, and mirin all depend on one mold: Aspergillus oryzae. Japan declared it a national microbe.

buildup.text: Koji mold produces powerful enzymes that break down proteins into amino acids and starches into sugars.

discovery.text: Those amino acids create umami—the deep, savory flavor that defines Japanese cuisine.

twist.text: Western chefs discovered koji and now use it to age steaks, make rapid miso, and create new fermented sauces.

climax.text: Koji is the wild card species—closely related to toxic Aspergillus flavus. Evolution separated delicious from deadly.

punchline.text: One mold built an entire cuisine. Koji is Japan's invisible chef.

quiz.question: What does koji mold produce that creates umami flavor?
options: Enzymes that break proteins into amino acids
